description: Compute logarithms to any base using the change-of-base formula. Get log, natural log (ln), log10 and log2 of any positive number.

faqs.a: log_b(x) answers the question: to what power must the base b be raised to get x? For example, log_2(8) = 3 because 2^3 = 8.

faqs.q: Why must the input be positive?
faqs.a: Real-valued logarithms are only defined for positive numbers, and the base must be positive and not equal to 1. This is a property of the exponential function, not a limitation of the tool.
The natural logarithm uses base e (approximately 2.71828). It appears throughout calculus, compound growth and science, and this tool shows it alongside every result.

faqs.q: How is a custom base computed?
faqs.a: With the change-of-base formula: log_b(x) = ln(x) / ln(b). This is exactly how the calculator evaluates any base you enter.

howto: Enter the positive number x you want the logarithm of.
Choose a base: 10, e, 2, or type your own custom base.
Read log_b(x) instantly, plus ln(x), log10(x) and log2(x) for reference.
The change-of-base working is shown so you can verify the result.
title: Logarithm Calculator
